edges.label: Green was CIA's monitor for the SRI psychoenergetics work
edges.note: Green served in CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence, Life Sciences Division, and has stated he was the officer to whom anomalous-phenomena reporting was routed.

edges.label: CENTER LANE succeeded GRILL FLAME after the codename was compromised
edges.note: Codeword churn on compromise is standard practice; the effort was continuous across the renaming.

edges.label: Puthoff founded and led the SRI psychoenergetics programme
edges.note: CIA's Office of Technical Service funded the work from 1972; it was later sponsored by Army INSCOM and DIA under successive codenames.

edges.label: SRI methodology transferred into the Army/DIA GRILL FLAME programme
edges.note: GRILL FLAME formalised operational remote viewing at Fort Meade using the SRI protocols, with SRI continuing as the research contractor.

edges.label: DIA sponsored the remote-viewing effort 1986-1995
edges.note: DIA's prior experience running an unacknowledged programme in a ridiculed domain is the institutional precedent for its 2008 AAWSAP contract.

b.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995

edges.label: SUN STREAK became STARGATE, terminated 1995
edges.note: CIA compiled and released roughly 12,000 pages of the programme record in 1995 after the American Institutes for Research evaluation.
